notes: Grades: the integer in cells like "C- (72)", "B+ 87", "**C+ (78)**"; the letter is ignored (mismatches with the common scale are listed in grade_letter_mismatches, informational only).
Greenfield grades: the addendum "new" value where the addendum re-grades that ticket in that batch, otherwise the first-round grade. kl2a1aa and syem have no addendum, so greenfield = first-round.

problem = first sentence of the "concern" cell (empty for LANDED-SOUND); evidence = first sentence of the "evidence" cell plus every other file:line ref in it; critique = first sentence of the "approach critique" cell. `source` points at the full row.

verdict is the base token; any qualifier such as "(intentional)" or "(landed, then regressed)" is in verdict_note. verdict_greenfield differs only where an addendum changed a verdict (standalone ct-oc2g).
epic = the ticket file's parent:, or the ticket itself when its type is epic and it has no parent; null for standalone tickets.
syem rows come from syem-verdicts.md (merged from syem-part-*.md by syem-merge.py); d8z3a rows from d8z3a-verdicts.md (merged from its fork files); kl2a1aa from both tables in kl2a1aa-verdicts.md.
ct-czsd (epic, in_progress) is graded only in prose and the czsd source excludes it from averages, so it is in untabled_epics, not tickets.
d8z3b repeats the epic ct-d8z3 (its averages cover 23 rows), so ct-d8z3 has two entries, both duplicate: true.
ct-csjp/ct-lcbc/ct-mpsp/ct-tcfg (congressional-tech) and ss-csjp/ss-lcbc/ss-mpsp/ss-tcfg (docspec-rs) are different tickets that share a suffix.
raw_data_risk is true when the ticket appears in a raw_risks entry's tickets list. Positive safeguards from the risk tables are in raw_protections and do not set raw_data_risk.
150 of 506 first-round grade cells carry a letter that disagrees with the common scale for their number (for example "C+ (72)"); the number was used.

raw_risks.detail: Outside pytest, iter_states_for reads a local adoption state.parquet when its row count matches, and changed() reads .cache/docspec-catalog/captures-0.parquet when schema and row-group counts match. R2Store.read serves receipts/ and bodies/sha256/ from a local cache_dir that raw_sync sets, so capture readback can compare against the cache, not R2. No digest checks; tests skip the branch via PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST.
raw_risks.evidence: retention/raw_storage.py:654-672; retention/source_capture_inputs.py:61-74; retention/catalog_raw_updates.py:591; retention/source_replay.py:229,260; retention/r2.py:247-255,272-278; cli/raw_sync.py:323
raw_risks.reachable_notes: On any machine holding those files; in capture runs with --native-config. The recovery import sets no cache_dir.
raw_risks.severity: mi03a ranks it second; standalone: medium

raw_risks.title: Native-manifest disk cache can skip raw-state manifest uploads
raw_risks.detail: The upload is skipped when a cached file of the same size exists, and the cache is not keyed by bucket. A cache_dir shared across buckets could leave raw-state manifests (selected through indexes/raw.json) unuploaded.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: d8z3b: cache_dir is opt-in. standalone RR06 notes raw_sync sets cache_dir; whether one is shared across buckets is unverified.

raw_risks.title: Raw-state selector rewritten in place with no old-vs-new value check (ct-dmca)
raw_risks.detail: upgrade-source-rules evolves the raw URL-state leaves (outcome, sha256, body_key provenance), adds a scalar backfill group, then publishes a new raw selector over RAW_KEY. The only check is a selector readback. Old native versions stay immutable, so this is a provenance-pointer risk, not byte loss.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Through raw_sync --upgrade-source-rules whenever the stored state schema differs from STATE_SCHEMA.

raw_risks.title: Retention planner would mark raw objects reclaimable (ct-a70m, ct-qdkd)
raw_risks.detail: The planner expects path/protected/status/reasons, but the engine returns objects:[{object, blocker}], so engine-protected objects read as reclaimable. It also treats anything not protected by a caller pin, engine status or path match as reclaimable (the engine reports unknown objects as "unmatched"). With removal_id set it requests a native removal plan.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: The CLI passes no objects and no removal_id. The Python client has no method for /retention/removal/execute. It turns dangerous once deletion is wired to this plan.

raw_risks.title: Automatic retries of raw-table commits whose outcome is unknown (ct-3faj regression)
raw_risks.detail: run_table and update_table retry 3 times (1+2+4 s) when stderr contains "commit state is unknown", "remote_unconfirmed", "gateway" or 502/503/504. This breaks ct-3faj's "no automatic retry" AC, and the substring match can hit hex digests in refusal messages. Raw capture and state leaves on R2 go through run_table. Native operation-id idempotency probably makes replay safe, but the policy was never qualified.
raw_risks.evidence: packages/docspec_client/src/docspec_client/client.py:501-552,720-770; raw writers retention/raw_storage.py:1066,1075,1217 (introduced by ct-2ukk commits 48137619, 71e5c5fd)

raw_risks.title: Raw-state Updates depend on engine key-pruning correctness (ct-csyg, ct-tuez)
raw_risks.detail: Hand-rolled key pruning decides which raw-state rows an Update replaces; skipping a file that holds a key could leave duplicate or stale state rows. Pruning also trusts 64-127-byte string bounds, and raw captures are keyed by 64-hex sha256 and a 74-byte body_key. Bounds are used only as intervals, truncated Parquet min/max stay valid endpoints, and oracle tests cover it.
raw_risks.evidence: rs:src/engine/key_pruning.rs:735-746; rs:src/engine/write/compaction.rs:66-73; rs:src/storage.rs:97,451; rs:tests/update_pruning.rs:283; retention/raw_storage.py:1187-1233; oracle tests rs:381108c
raw_risks.reachable_notes: mi03a: narrowly, only after RR08 runs. standalone: in raw-source-sync and recovery import.

raw_risks.title: Qualification data written into the raw (and public) bucket (ct-3180)
raw_risks.detail: The ct-3180 qualification wrote under s3://congressional-tech-raw/__r2_data_catalog/docspec-qualification-20261019/. It is isolated by owned prefix and not on the public allowlist, but the practice should stop.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: One-off.

raw_risks.title: Owner close kills a draining host (ct-bt1q)
raw_risks.detail: SIGINT, then SIGTERM after about 5 s, then SIGKILL. Admitted raw writes may be cut off; native recovery state and retained producer inputs survive.

raw_risks.title: The engine that writes raw provenance is self-attested (ct-ugqq, ct-oxg6)
raw_risks.detail: Setup checks the downloaded artifact only against its own descriptor, never against QUALIFIED_DOCSPEC_RUNTIME, and the raw capture workflow then writes state into the raw bucket. The digest stops tampering, not staleness or a wrong version. The Oct 20-24 stale pin failed loudly, but quiet writes from an older engine cannot be ruled out without seeing R2.

raw_risks.title: Raw-state update can silently drop its merge policy
raw_risks.detail: On TypeError it retries without merge, which would turn LATEST_OR_BACKFILL into plain key replacement and could null body_key/sha256 provenance. Delete the fallback.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Not with the current client, which accepts merge. Adjacent to ct-m9td/ct-xq1y, out of batch.

raw_risks.title: news_lake append-ID uniqueness hole (ct-qkvr)
raw_risks.detail: Probe P2: a fresh DocSpecLake on the same workspace accepts a re-append of an existing identity_decision id with a new recorded_at and changed content (2 rows stored).
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Pilot only, local workspace. It becomes a raw-provenance bug only if news capture goes live.

raw_risks.title: Forgeable VerifiedFile proofs (ct-fw0m, ct-1dsp, ct-3djs)
raw_risks.detail: custody.py issues a "verified" proof without hashing. The only production positional constructions are in derived catalog preparation; raw writers use hashing file_identity and MD5-checked uploads. It is a trap: the first raw writer to build VerifiedFile(path, sha, size) gets a free proof.

raw_risks.title: Raw recovery receipts and audit evidence kept only in untracked output/
raw_risks.detail: Raw recovery batch receipts live under untracked output/ (for example output/corpus-retry-20261015/publication-batches/*). Any that are not also in the R2 raw archive tables are one cleanup away from loss. The batch audit evidence folders are already gone.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Not verified; belongs to the corpus_recovery preservation owner.

raw_risks.title: Recovery-acceptance mapping is mutable provenance under the derived prefix
raw_risks.detail: viewer-publications/recoveries/accepted.json is replaced in place with IfMatch and R2 keeps no history; the local before/after copies were pruned. Each batch merges with the remote copy and keeps "fresh edits/deletions" that may be in no retained batch. A cleanup of viewer-publications/ could delete it as "derived". The same associations also land in raw import receipts as source_associations.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Every recovery publication (mapping phase).
raw_risks.severity: d8z3b: low-medium; standalone: CANNOT-VERIFY whether the file counts as provenance

raw_risks.title: Preflight signs GETs with the full write credential
raw_risks.detail: Contained by a key allowlist and by refusing redirects, so Authorization is never forwarded. A read-only token is the platform primitive.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Read-only in practice.

raw_risks.title: Legacy capture/state Parquet may be raw provenance until its receipts are confirmed in R2
raw_risks.detail: 3,909,134 legacy capture rows reference 2,289 distinct receipts/ keys with 0 nulls, so the tables can be derived from receipts only if all of those exist in R2 (CANNOT-VERIFY offline). Nothing writes or deletes the tables now. List receipts/ once, confirm keys and line counts, and keep the tables immutable and backed up until then.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: No writer or deleter is reachable; receipt existence is unverified.

raw_risks.title: Engine remote exact-key deletion has a small TOCTOU window
raw_risks.detail: Deletion is scope-checked, size- and BLAKE3-verified and runs through an expiring HEAD/DELETE-only actor, with a gap between the digest check and the delete. It cannot reach receipts/ or bodies/ while the RR03 scope check holds.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Engine code only; the consumer plans removals but never executes them.

raw_risks.title: False custody record for every raw-* engine write (post-pin HEAD)
raw_risks.detail: On remote, initial Builds of raw-*, catalog-*, obs-* and source-observations-* record the remote input ObjectRef without uploading the bytes, then read the local file; availability and Deep checks skip those names. It is compiled only under cfg(not(test)), so no test runs it. No raw bytes are lost, but the engine's record is wrong and inventory, restore or removal closures over these inputs will fail.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Yes in a HEAD release build against R2; not in the pinned c949c67.

raw_risks.title: Deferred lifecycle commits hold protections only in memory (post-pin HEAD)
raw_risks.detail: Protections and phase records stay in memory until the final commit and flush errors are discarded. A crash leaves orphan objects inside the owned prefix; nothing is deleted.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: HEAD production build; not in the pin.

raw_risks.title: Sweeping local reclaim fails open (ss-g9sn)
raw_risks.detail: It unlinks anything under <retained>/<dataset>/ outside the live closure, and the head-reference walk fails open (unwrap_or_default). It is gated to local storage and must never be enabled remotely.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Not for R2: gated to local storage.
raw_risks.severity: low; the most dangerous pattern in the engine

raw_risks.title: Retained producer input deleted on errors raised after admission (ct-0n0y residual)
raw_risks.detail: pre_admission is derived from the error kind: any serde error becomes invalid_json, a 422 with pre_admission=true, which the engine also raises after admission. cleanup_safe then lets shutil.rmtree remove the retained producer input. The staged input can be rebuilt from receipts already written immutably.

raw_risks.title: Large payload cells are re-sliced and copied on write
raw_risks.detail: These are copies of bodies/, not the originals.

raw_risks.title: Import code-provenance record misses the raw-writing modules (ct-esm4)
raw_risks.detail: The import dispatcher's hand-written pin list leaves out docspec_client (the transport behind retention/docspec.py) and congress_shared.custody/storage. That code writes the raw native datasets and indexes/raw.json, so the provenance record and runtime check miss it.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Every recovery import run.
raw_risks.severity: medium (provenance gap, not data loss); standalone top problem

raw_risks.title: news_lake production writer skips fencing and fsync (ct-1h4g, ct-a1aa)
raw_risks.detail: DocSpecLake.commit_records never checks the fencing epoch (fenced_commit has no callers), so a stale writer can commit tables and rewrite committed state. Manifest and state are written with fsync=False before the release is marked available. The crash matrix covers only the Iceberg oracle.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Not stated by kl2a1aa. Other batches describe news_lake as a local pilot that never touches R2.

raw_risks.title: body_key provenance became code, not data
raw_risks.detail: Raw tables no longer store body_key; it is derived from sha256 at read time. f2fea711 switched the derivation to .pdf for about 22 h (with a test asserting the bug) before 2400dbd1 reverted it. _prepare_bodies persisted body:+body_key entries into the raw-bodies routing index, so scan it and anything else persisted Oct 22 20:16 to Oct 23 18:44 for .pdf keys. Keep the golden test.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: The bad derivation is reverted; entries persisted during the window are unscanned.

raw_risks.title: C5 restricted-text gate leaks expired text on subset reads (ct-a3le, ct-5yof)
raw_risks.detail: Expiry is computed only from news.captures rows present in the read, so a read without captures exports text whose capture has expired.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Matters only once exports are published.

raw_risks.title: Raw capture receipts record the wrong stored_sha256 (ct-v9ua)
raw_risks.detail: The surviving legacy round-trip writes stored_sha256 = sha256 on every new gzip capture; it should be the digest of the stored gzip object. corpus_recovery trusts the field. Fix now, then re-derive stored_sha256 for affected rows from the R2 objects.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Every gzip capture appended since Oct 22.

raw_risks.title: Invented provenance in the weekly retention mirror (ct-q29c)
raw_risks.detail: observed_at is hardcoded to 2026-09-27, outcome is "present" on every row, there are congress=118 and 1970 sentinels, payload_json was dropped, and bodies are staged only in an ephemeral workspace. The source pipeline-data still exists, so a mirror is corrupted, not the originals. Leave nulls or delete the write-only mirror.

raw_risks.title: Raw-recovery --streamed-recovery mode cannot run (ct-fsbf)
raw_risks.detail: It raises TypeError on every call. It fails closed, so no data is harmed. Delete the mode or fix it with a CLI test.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: The mode is reachable and always fails closed.

raw_risks.title: export-pins --publish-to-r2 repoints a manifest in the raw bucket at nothing (ct-wxhg)
raw_risks.detail: It repoints viewer-publications/manifest.json in congressional-tech-raw at a manifest it never uploads, using placeholder defaults. The prefix is derived, but the bucket is shared with raw data. Delete the command.
raw_risks.reachable_notes: Not stated; the command exists. d8z3a notes this route writes only under viewer-publications/.

raw_protections.title: Publication key allowlist plus explicit write conditions (the raw firewall)
raw_protections.detail: GuardedPublicationClient.put_object writes only catalog-generations/, catalog-history/sha256/, indexes/processing/, viewer-publications/, indexes/native-manifests/ and indexes/catalog.json, and every write needs IfMatch or IfNoneMatch. No test sends a bodies/ key; the allowlist covers it anyway.

raw_protections.title: Second publication route confined to viewer-publications/
raw_protections.detail: export-pins --publish-to-r2 (ConditionalManifestPublisher) writes only under viewer-publications/releases/ and the manifest pointer. It treats 412 as success without comparing bytes, which can hide only a derived mismatch. See RR35 for its dangling-pointer bug.

raw_protections.title: put_derived_file limited to two catalog keys, create-only (ct-fw0m)
raw_protections.detail: require_derived_key allows only the two exact catalog table keys, and writes use IfNoneMatch="*".

raw_protections.title: Recovery-import admission is read-only and fails closed (ct-4r1c)
raw_protections.detail: Checks sealed-batch file pins, readiness against source-record coverage, import completion counts and the raw selector readback. Known defects (bare AttributeError, unnormalized pin paths) give false refusals, never false acceptance.

raw_protections.title: RecoveryGuard protects the raw import (ct-jl1m)
raw_protections.detail: Pins and rehashes inputs, checks protected object versions and observes capture writers. The real exclusion on indexes/raw.json is CAS.

raw_protections.title: Body-key shard must match its digest; exclusive local immutable writes (ct-qspb, ct-lu4i)
raw_protections.detail: ct-qspb requires a body key's shard to match its digest before an accepted mapping is written; ct-lu4i made local immutable writes use exclusive os.link.

raw_protections.title: Producer-input custody on unknown outcomes for raw-state writes (ct-m9td, ct-q968, ct-3faj)
raw_protections.detail: request.json and the producer Parquet are kept on an unknown outcome; raw paths use the default stream_ipc=False. Caveat: the IPC path has no custody and is reachable only from news_lake today, so keep raw writers off it.

raw_protections.title: Orphan receipts are re-applied on every run (ct-365w)
raw_protections.detail: Receipts are written immutably first, then native selection runs; orphans are re-applied each run. The O(history) listing covers about 2.3k receipt files (about 3 LIST pages); bound it by date prefix if it grows, do not remove it.

raw_protections.title: Immutable, verified raw writes
raw_protections.detail: Raw bodies and receipts are written with IfNoneMatch="*", uploads are MD5-verified, and corpus_recovery checked_put reads back exactly. These predate czsd: existing_body_info (43f112ef, Oct 1), immutable receipt batches (931500d9, Oct 5), checked_put (a2e25550, Oct 15).

raw_protections.title: Engine remote scope check and create-only writes
raw_protections.detail: Every remote put/delete/stat in objects.rs goes through scope.key (bucket match plus owned-prefix match), and writes use if_not_exists(true). drop_table never purges. docspec calls this the only raw boundary in the code.

raw_protections.title: No application path deletes R2 raw objects
raw_protections.detail: mi03a: no batch item deletes R2 raw objects and no Python path executes a native removal (compaction runs only from news_lake, which is local). standalone: no R2 delete in corpus_recovery, viewer_publication, news_lake or docspec_client. d8z3b: no delete_object/delete_objects calls in its code paths.
